claims: The Artemis II spacecraft will travel at speeds reaching roughly 24,000 to 25,000 miles per hour (approx. 40,000 km/h) during critical phases of its mission, such as Earth reentry.
The Orion capsule achieves a speed equivalent to over 11 miles per second to break free of Earth's orbital pull and head toward the Moon.
During initial ascent, the SLS rocket reaches speeds of around 17,500 mph (roughly 28,000 km/h) before the core stage separates.
During trans-lunar injection, the upper stage boosts the craft to over 22,000 mph to send it toward the Moon.
The spacecraft will hit the Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (approx. 40,000 kph) as it returns from the Moon during reentry.
During splashdown, parachutes will slow the capsule to approximately 17 mph for a landing in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission is expected to cover a total of 685,000 miles.
